programme: ZBTB18, SATB2 and TSHZ3 converge on BMP-SMAD-responsive differentiation targets: ZBTB18 drives the canonical BMP/SMAD target genes ID1-ID4 (plus RELN/ROBO1/SLIT3 axon-guidance genes), SATB2 sits on BMP-driven epithelial differentiation (its target set spans the EMT/stemness circuit SNAI1, SNAI2, ZEB1, CDH1/CDH2, CD44, PROM1, MYC alongside the BMP-organoid differentiation programme documented for it), and TSHZ3 targets BMP4 itself together with the myogenic differentiation genes MYOCD and MYOG. Together they read as a BMP-SMAD-gated switch between proliferative/EMT and terminally differentiated epithelial or smooth-muscle states.
role_in_a: In head-and-neck squamous epithelium, BMP-SMAD signalling normally enforces keratinocyte terminal differentiation against proliferative/EMT drive; if this axis is disrupted, SATB2's EMT-stemness target module (SNAI1/2, ZEB1, CDH1/CDH2, CD44, PROM1, MYC) becomes the plausible route to invasive, dedifferentiated OSCC.
role_in_b: In colonic epithelium and gut smooth muscle, BMP signalling drives colonocyte lineage commitment (the process the SATB2/organoid paper directly documents) and, via TSHZ3-BMP4-MYOCD/MYOG, smooth-muscle differentiation relevant to gut motility — a plausible substrate for the epithelial and motor disturbances implicated in IBS.
shared_axis: Both head-and-neck squamous epithelium and colonic epithelium/enteric smooth muscle reuse the same BMP-SMAD differentiation toolkit to hold cells in a terminally differentiated state against proliferative or mesenchymal drift; if ZBTB18, SATB2 and TSHZ3 mark the same BMP-responsive checkpoint in both tissues, disrupted BMP output would be the shared node — though this may just be the same developmental module used independently in two unrelated organs rather than a disease-linking mechanism.
reasoning: The three factors form a nameable BMP-SMAD differentiation module from their target identities, but nothing in the record documents head-and-neck cancer and IBS sharing this axis, and the pairing has no obvious anatomical or clinical basis. Support is weak: only SATB2 has a directly relevant retrieved paper (about organoid differentiation, not either disease), ZBTB18 — the strongest concordant factor at 158/184 — has zero evidence in either disease, and TSHZ3's only evidence is an Open Targets percentile rather than literature.
support: PMID 28648364 — shows BMP pathway activation drives differentiation of pluripotent stem cells into colonic organoids, placing SATB2's BMP-responsive differentiation role in colon-relevant tissue (not IBS as a disease specifically); no PMIDs place ZBTB18 or TSHZ3 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: Knock down or overexpress ZBTB18, SATB2 and TSHZ3 in matched oral/OSCC keratinocyte and colonic organoid models and measure BMP-target induction (ID1-4, BMP4) and differentiation markers; if the direction of BMP-responsive differentiation moves independently (or oppositely) between the two tissue models rather than concordantly, the shared-axis claim fails. Directly assaying SATB2/TSHZ3 expression or binding in HNC tumor tissue and finding no signal would also undercut the claim that this axis extends to the HNC side.
caveats: Tissue pairing is colorectal|head_neck — embryologically and anatomically distinct epithelia, so any shared BMP-differentiation link is a shared developmental module reused in different organs, not evidence of shared disease biology. 184 patient-group comparisons come from only 1 independent cohort pair, so high concordance (ZBTB18 158/184, SATB2 116/184, TSHZ3 107/184) reflects robustness across subgroup slicing of one cohort pairing, not independent replication. SMAD6 also sits on BMP/EMT biology and has direct HNC evidence (PMID 38539520, EMT in OSCC lymph-node metastasis) but is marked discordant, meaning its effect direction differs between the two diseases — this was excluded from the carrying set but suggests BMP-SMAD output may actually run in opposite directions across the two settings, which should temper this account. Tissue-generic exclusions removed likely master regulators of gut/head-neck epithelium before ranking, so an obviously-missing epithelial regulator is expected, not an oversight. Single-view exclusions (DLX3, NHLH2, ZNF205, FOXD2, MYC, PGR, MECOM) are unrelated to this account; DLX3 appears only as a downstream SMAD6 target, not as a candidate factor.
